gui.villager-news-addon-port.translation:
Subtitles work like subtitle files for a movie. No resource pack is needed.

Click Open subtitles folder below. It opens config/villager-news-addon-port/subtitles in your Minecraft folder. Every language of the mod is a file there, such as en_us.json or tr_tr.json.

To add a language:
1. Copy en_us.json and name the copy after a Minecraft language code, such as de_de.json or fr_fr.json.
2. Set "language" to the name of your language, then translate each line in "subtitles" and each speaker name in "names". "signs" is the text on the signs villagers carry. Do not change the keys. Long lines are split over several keys, so translate each part in its own key.
3. Come back to the settings and choose your language. Auto uses your game language when a subtitle file for it exists.

You can edit any file and your changes are kept. Delete a file to remove its language. English always stays as the fallback. Files you have not changed are updated with the mod.

Optional: an AI coding assistant can draft a translation for you. Give it ai_translation_prompt.md from the same folder together with the mod's source code, then have a native speaker check the result.

Lines you leave out are shown in English. example_language.json shows the format in short. Resource packs can also add subtitles at assets/villager-news-addon-port/subtitles/<code>.json.

handbook.villager-news-addon-port.overvi: Reactive Dialogue
Villagers react to nearby mobs, blocks, player actions, trading, damage and plenty more. Try doing things around them and listen for a response.
Animations
Villagers are fully animated with custom movement, expressive voiceline animations and lip sync that brings their dialogue to life.
Villager Styles
Choose between Vanilla, Actions & Stuff and Actions & Stuff: Flat Style Villagers in Settings to match the look of your world.
Conversations
Villagers don't just react to you. They can interact with each other too, with conversations and unique exchanges between Villagers.
Reaction Categories
Reactions cover player actions, mobs, building, trading, Villager life, damage, world events, conversations and plenty more. Browse the Triggers & Reactions Guide to discover them all.
Player Reputation

Villagers remember how you treat them. Trading and curing Villagers improve your reputation, while hurting or killing them lowers it. Villagers will even gossip about you with each other, changing how they react to you.
Special Villagers
One of each special Villager News character spawns in your world. Explore different Villages to find them and trade for their unique items.
Wandering Traders
Wandering Traders have their own dialogue for trading, sold-out stock, successful deals and plenty more.
Baby Villagers
Baby Villagers have their own reactions and animations.
Rare Lines
Rare Lines are longer, more unusual and over-the-top reactions. Use the Rare Villager Lines setting to disable them or make them more common.
Chattiness
Use Villager Chattiness in Settings to control how often Villagers speak, from completely silent to extremely chatty.
Subtitles
Enable Show Subtitles in Settings if you want spoken lines displayed on screen.

handbook.villager-news-addon-port.genera: Triggers are actions, events or situations Villagers can notice. Reactions are the dialogue and animations they may respond with.
Most reactions require a Villager to be nearby or able to see what is happening. Different triggers can have different detection requirements.
Reactions use cooldowns to keep dialogue feeling natural. Repeating the same or similar actions may not trigger another reaction immediately.
Not every trigger will cause a Villager to react every time. Cooldowns, distance, visibility, context and Chattiness can all affect whether a reaction plays.
Some reactions depend on additional conditions such as the Villager's profession, age, surroundings, your reputation or what is happening nearby.
Many triggers have multiple possible reactions, so Villagers won't always respond to the same situation in exactly the same way.
Villager Chattiness controls how frequently Villagers speak. Lower settings make reactions less frequent, while higher settings make Villagers more talkative.
Some reactions include longer and more unusual Rare Lines. Their frequency can be adjusted separately using Rare Villager Lines in Settings.
